A2ACardDiscoveryResponse.description:
Response shape for the public discovery endpoint.

Brutor-specific wrapper around the v1.0 Agent Card. The wrapper
carries registry metadata (stable `id`, `trust_tier`, detected
dialect) that the spec doesn't cover — external verifiers that
only understand the v1.0 spec body read the `card` field and
ignore the wrapper.

The `card` field is **always** a v1.0-shaped AgentCard (see
[`a2a_v1::AgentCard`]). Cards stored in the v0.3 form are
translated on-the-fly via [`a2a_v1::translator::translate_v03_to_v1`],
so a partner never sees the dialect the gateway happens to have
at rest.

a2a_version.description:
`"1.0"` if the card was either stored as or translated into v1.0
shape. `"0.3"` if translation was skipped (never surfaces today —
we always translate — but kept in the schema for forward-compat).

card.description: The v1.0 Agent Card body. Verifiers consume only this field.

id.description:
Stable ULID — external agents pass this back as `target_card_id`
when invoking capabilities, so they never need to resolve names.

signature.description:
Legacy v0.3 flat signature fields — still populated from the
stored row during the v1.0 rollout so pre-v1.0 consumers don't
break. Under v1.0 rules the authoritative signatures live in
`card.signatures[]` and partners should key on those.

group_id.description: Optional group override for skill dispatch. Ignored by `noop`.

message.description:
Opaque message body passed to the handler. For `handler_type=skill`
this is mapped into `SkillExecuteRequest.input_params`.

target_card_id.description:
Stable card ID (not name). External callers get this from the
discovery response.

capability.description:
Dotted A2A capability name, e.g. `billing.refund`. Must match
one of the capabilities advertised on the card.

message.description: The A2A message body forwarded verbatim to the remote agent.

target_card_id.description:
The gateway's internal ID of the target Agent Card.
(Not the card's `id` field — the DB primary key.)

outcome_id.description:
The outcome the run ended in, as declared in the AI
System's contract: `<outcome>` or `<outcome>.<variant>`, each part
`[a-z0-9_-]{1,48}`. Judged against the active contract's catalogue;
a malformed value is refused with 400.

state.description:
How the run ended. Omit to let the gateway infer it.

The one value worth sending is `exhausted`: it is the canonical
"my agent looped until it ran out of iterations" signal and the
gateway has no way to observe it.

accepted.description: GenAI spans turned into step rows.

aiSystemId.description: The AI System the runs were attributed to, if any.

runs.description: Run ids (`otel:<trace id>`) the accepted spans belong to.

skipped.description: Spans in the export that were not GenAI evidence (kept as topology).

PartialSuccess.description:
OTLP's own partial-success envelope, so a collector treats the inlet
like any other OTLP endpoint.

probe_type.description:
One of `"catalog"`, `"endpoint"`, `"synthetic"`. Drives the
`endpoint_category` tag on the proxy_metric row so the
per-category breakdown attributes probe traffic correctly.

reopened.description:
True when this call re-closed an already-finalized run, which
happens when a step arrives late. Surfaced rather than hidden so a
client that double-sends can tell.

approval_token.description:
One-time approval token(s) for retrying a skill execution that was
held for a person, for a caller that cannot set the
`X-Approval-Token` header. Several tokens are separated by commas.

allowed_tools.description:
Pre-approved tools for this skill execution.
The calling agent should restrict LLM tool use to this list.

max_tool_calls_per_execution.description:
Maximum tool calls allowed per execution (from group governance).
The calling agent should enforce this limit during execution.

output.description:
Output produced by the skill's scripts when the gateway dispatched the
execution to the runner inline (REST path). Present only when the
execution actually ran to completion; absent for a pure agent-handoff. Governed by skill_output
guardrails before it reaches this field.

recommended_model.description: Recommended LLM model for this skill execution.

skill_prompt.description:
Expanded skill prompt (SKILL.md content).
Inject this into the LLM conversation as system/user context.

edition.description:
Which edition answers: `community` or `enterprise`. What the process
is composed of (`services::edition::Composition`), not a build flag.

404.description: Tenant unknown, A2A disabled, or no signing key yet

get.summary: Public JWK Set for a tenant's Agent Card signatures

get.description: Unauthenticated. Returns the verbatim card JSON + signature block for external verifiers. 404 if the tenant has A2A disabled, the card is disabled, or the card has been revoked.

404.description: Card not available for public discovery

post.description: OTLP/HTTP **JSON** `ExportTraceServiceRequest`. Spans carrying GenAI semantic-convention attributes (`gen_ai.operation.name` = chat | text_completion | generate_content | embeddings | execute_tool | invoke_agent) become step rows of a run keyed on the trace id; every other span is skipped. Ingested evidence is recorded as *reported* (`source = otel`, `chain_integrity = observed_external`): the gateway did not witness it and applied no control. Attribute the run with `X-Brutor-AI-System` or the `brutor.ai_system` resource attribute. Protobuf bodies are refused with 415.

400.description: Body is not an OTLP JSON export

413.description: Too many spans in one request

415.description: Protobuf is not accepted; use http/json

post.summary: Ingest OpenTelemetry GenAI spans as run evidence

get.description:
Serves one stored file through a link the gateway signed. Clients do not build these links: `GET /v1/proxy/files/{file_id}/url` returns one (when the gateway's media store is the filesystem one; with the S3 store it returns a presigned bucket URL instead), and the client fetches it as it is, path and query unchanged. The link is opaque.

No credential is sent: the link is the credential. It names one file, is bound to that file's tenant, and stops working at `expires`; changing any part of it invalidates it.

Every link that does not open a file (unsigned, tampered, expired, malformed, a key outside the store, a file that is gone, or a gateway whose media store is not the filesystem one) answers the same `404` with no body that tells the cases apart.

parameters.description: The stored file's key, as the link carries it (several path segments).
parameters.name: key

parameters.description: When the link stops working, in Unix seconds, as the link carries it.
parameters.name: expires

parameters.description: The gateway's signature over the link, as the link carries it.
parameters.name: signature

200.description: The file. `Content-Type` is the type recorded when the file was stored. Images (except SVG), audio and video are served `inline` so that ``, `

Cache-Control.description: `private, max-age=` the seconds left until the link expires

Content-Disposition.description: `inline; filename="…"` for images (not SVG), audio and video; `attachment; filename="…"` otherwise

404.description: The link does not open a file. One answer for every reason (see the description).

500.description: The file exists and the link is valid, but the store could not read it.

get.summary: Download a file through a signed link

delete.description:
**Canonical entrypoint** for talking to a registered MCP server through the
gateway. This is the URL that MCP clients should use for normal operation.

### What it does

- Proxies JSON-RPC methods (`initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`,
  `prompts/list`, `resources/read`, …).
- Supports Streamable HTTP transport — the gateway negotiates between a one-shot
  JSON response and an SSE stream based on the `Accept` header.
- Injects credentials. If the MCP server is registered with `auth_type=oauth`
  and a refresh token, the gateway attaches a fresh Bearer token to the upstream
  call. Clients do **not** need to manage MCP-server credentials themselves.
- Enforces group access and usage quotas (call count, daily budget).
- Logs every call to `proxy_logs` with tenant, group, method, capability,
  upstream latency, and result.

### Endpoint-path handling

The gateway **automatically appends** the server's configured `mcp_endpoint_path`
(set at registration time) when forwarding to the upstream. Clients **must not**
include it in the URL — doing so produces a doubled path on the upstream and
typically returns 404/405.

Example: a server registered with `base_url=https://upstream.example.com`
and `mcp_endpoint_path=/mcp` is reached at:

| Client sends             | Gateway forwards to             |
|--------------------------|---------------------------------|
| `/v1/proxy/mcp/{id}`     | `https://upstream.example.com/mcp` |

### Required headers

| Header | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | `Bearer sk_brutor_api_…` | Group-scoped API key |
| `X-Tenant-ID` | `<tenant-slug>` | Required for tenant routing |
| `Accept` | `application/json, text/event-stream` | Streamable HTTP requires **both** — sending only `application/json` may produce 405/406 |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` | For JSON-RPC bodies |

### Related endpoints

- For OAuth discovery (`.well-known/*`) or REST-style sub-paths, see
  `POST /v1/proxy/mcp/{server_id}/{path}`.

### Example: initialize handshake

```bash
curl -X POST "https://gateway.example.com/v1/proxy/mcp/{server_id}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_brutor_api_…" \
  -H "X-Tenant-ID: my-tenant" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -d '{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 1,
    "method": "initialize",
    "params": {
      "protocolVersion": "2025-06-18",
      "clientInfo": {"name": "my-client", "version": "1.0"},
      "capabilities": {}
    }
  }'
```

200.description: MCP server response (JSON or SSE stream)

403.description: Access denied — user's group does not have access to this MCP server

404.description: MCP server not found or disabled

413.description: Request body over the MCP payload limit (`data.max_payload_size_mb`, never above 10 MiB)

429.description: MCP usage limit exceeded — a quota, a frequency limit or a concurrency allowance (JSON-RPC error, `error.data.limit_type`), or the limits cannot be read (`limits_unavailable`)

502.description: The MCP server's answer is over the payload limit (JSON-RPC `payload_too_large`) or broke off

504.description: The MCP server did not answer within the call's timeout

delete.description:
Proxies requests to a **sub-path** on a registered MCP server.

> ⚠ For normal JSON-RPC + Streamable HTTP calls, use the canonical endpoint
> `POST /v1/proxy/mcp/{server_id}` — the gateway appends the server's configured
> `mcp_endpoint_path` itself, so clients **must not** include it in the URL.

This endpoint exists for **two specific use cases**, picked apart by the first
character of `{path}`:

### 1. OAuth discovery (primary use case)

Paths beginning with `.` (e.g. `.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`,
`.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`) are rewritten to hit the MCP
server's **origin**, *dropping* the configured `mcp_endpoint_path`.

This is mandated by:
- [RFC 8414](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8414) — OAuth 2.0 Authorization
  Server Metadata
- [RFC 9728](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9728) — OAuth 2.0 Protected
  Resource Metadata

Discovery metadata is a **resource-level** concept and must live at the server
origin. For an MCP server with `base_url=https://example.com/api/mcp` and
`mcp_endpoint_path=/mcp`, the discovery document is fetched from
`https://example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` — never from
`…/api/mcp/.well-known/...`.

**Examples:**
- `GET /v1/proxy/mcp/{server_id}/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`
- `GET /v1/proxy/mcp/{server_id}/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`

### 2. REST-style MCP servers (escape hatch)

Any other sub-path is appended to `base_url` verbatim. Used by non-standard
MCP implementations that expose plain HTTP endpoints rather than (or in
addition to) the JSON-RPC entrypoint. Rarely needed — modern Streamable HTTP
clients should target `/v1/proxy/mcp/{server_id}` instead.

**Example:** `GET /v1/proxy/mcp/{server_id}/tools/list-rest`

### Required headers

| Header | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | `Bearer sk_brutor_api_…` | Group-scoped API key |
| `X-Tenant-ID` | `<tenant-slug>` | Required for tenant routing |
| `Accept` | `application/json, text/event-stream` | Streamable HTTP requires **both** |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` | For JSON-RPC bodies |

Answers 200 when the run has ended (`execution_status` is `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`), and 202 when the call is held for a person: the body is then the approval envelope (`approval_required: true`, no `execution_id`), and the same call is retried with the approval token.
